chunks: It is narrated from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī that he said:

When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم married Fāṭimah to ʿAlī عليه السلام, some people from Quraysh came to him and said: “You have married ʿAlī with a paltry dowry.” So he said to them:
“It was not I who married ʿAlī, but rather Allah, Mighty and Majestic, married him on the night that I was taken on the Night Journey at Sidrat al-Muntahā.”

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the lote tree: “Scatter.” So it scattered pearls and jewels upon the wide-eyed maidens, and they exchanged them as gifts among themselves and boasted of them, saying: “This is from the scattering of Fāṭimah, daughter of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.”
Then when the night of the wedding came, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم brought his gray mule and folded a cloak upon it, and said to Fāṭimah عليها السلام: “Mount.”

And he instructed Salmān, may Allah have mercy on him, to lead it, while the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم drove it from behind. Then while he was on part of the road, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم heard a sound, and there was Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام among seventy thousand, and Mīkāʾīl among seventy thousand. So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “What has brought you down to the earth?”

They said: “We have come to escort Fāṭimah عليها السلام to her husband.” And Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام proclaimed takbīr, and Mīkāʾīl عليه السلام proclaimed takbīr, and the angels proclaimed takbīr, and Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم proclaimed takbīr. Thus takbīr was established over brides from that night.

key_terms.الْجَوْهَرَ: jewels cast down as precious ornaments
key_terms.الْعَرَائِسِ: brides in the context of wedding custom
key_terms.سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى: the lote tree at the utmost boundary in the heavenly ascent
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الزِّفَافِ: the night of the bridal procession

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the marriage of Fāṭimah عليها السلام and ʿAlī عليه السلام and the origin of takbīr at weddings?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the heavenly dignity of the marriage of Fāṭimah عليها السلام and ʿAlī عليه السلام, presenting it as divinely ordained and honored by the angels. It also narrates the wedding procession and links the practice of takbīr at weddings to that blessed night.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4402 - It is narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari that he said:
When the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, married Sayyidah Fatimah {s.a} to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), peace be upon them, some people from Quraysh came to Him (sw) and said: "You have married Ali (as) with a trivial dowry."
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, replied to them:
"It was not I, who married Ali (as), but Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, married Him (as) to Her {s.a}.
On the night I was taken on the Night Journey to the Sidrat al-Muntaha (Lote Tree at the Utmost Boundary), Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the Lote Tree, 'Scatter your ornaments.' It then scattered pearls and jewels upon the maidens of Paradise, who exchanged them as gifts and took pride in them, saying, 'This is from the scattering for Sayyidah Fatimah {s.a}, the daughter of Muhammad (sw), peace be upon him and his family.'"
When the night of the wedding arrived, the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, brought his grey mule and covered it with a cloak. 
He (sw) said to Sayyidah Fatimah {s.a}, peace be upon her, "Mount it."
He (sw) then commanded Salman, may Allah (swt) have mercy on him, to lead it, while the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, walked behind it.
While they were on the way, the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, heard a sound and saw Archangel Jibril (Gabriel) (as), descending with seventy thousand angels, and Mika'il (Michael), peace be upon him, with seventy thousand angels.
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "What has brought you down to earth?"
They said: "We have come to escort Sayyida Fatimah {s.a}, peace be upon her, to her husband."
Archangel Jibril (as) proclaimed "Allahu Akbar" (Allah (swt) is the Greatest), and Mika'il, peace be upon him, followed with the same proclamation, as did the angels.
Then Muhammad (sw), peace be upon him and his family, also proclaimed "Allahu Akbar." From that night, the custom of proclaiming "Allahu Akbar" during weddings was established.
